CH1_PACK_SUMMARY: Three independent advanced cases combining access control, deployment recovery and counterevidence.
CH1_X01_ABSTRACTION: This independent challenge uses registered accounts, requests, files and observations. Other valid solutions and manual help remain available.
CH1_X01_BRIEF:
This is the first joint-response exercise. Receipt records are exposed to unrelated accounts, while sign-in failures repeat at the same entrance. Closing every entrance also removes legitimate citizen work. Verify receipt access and failed-attempt limits together under one configuration.

The original route needs separate ownership and per-account retry controls. The approved gateway has fixed delegation scopes and its own retry limit, so legitimate work may be migrated there instead. Observe the repeated-failure samples and verify a limiting response on the final sample. An account already tested may be limited on an earlier sample too. Another citizen must still be able to sign in.
The authorized work account is below. After connecting, the case tool shows current observations and permitted actions.

CH1_X01_CASE_FOREIGN_DIRECT: Unrelated Account at the Original Entrance
CH1_X01_CASE_FOREIGN_GATEWAY: Unrelated Account at the Approved Route
CH1_X01_DESK_NAME: A Door That Must Stay Open Desk
CH1_X01_GOAL: Preserve legitimate receipt access, staff work and sign-in while limiting unauthorized reads and repeated failures on both routes.
CH1_X01_HINT_1: Ownership and retry limits are separate controls. Fixing only one cannot satisfy every outcome.
CH1_X01_HINT_2: Failure samples at each entrance must be refused, with the final sample limited. Earlier limiting caused by your investigation is also a valid refusal. Legitimate sign-in uses a different account.
CH1_X01_HINT_3: Repair the original entrance, or close only that entrance and migrate legitimate receipt/sign-in work to the approved gateway. Keep the gateway open.
CH1_X01_LIMIT: This does not attack real servers or establish protection against every attack. Reading has no time penalty, and mistaken settings can be repaired.
CH1_X01_PRINCIPLE: Availability and authorization scope must be checked together. Retry limiting is an authentication outcome, distinct from the global alert indicator.
CH1_X01_REPLY: Legitimate citizen and staff work remains, while unrelated reads and repeated sign-ins are refused. The handoff records that real work survived, whichever entrance you chose. The next site proposes widening deployment permissions.
CH1_X01_TITLE: A Door That Must Stay Open

CH1_X02_BRIEF:
The deployment account cannot update its status file, so the night notice has stopped. A proposal would open both folder and file to everyone, including unrelated accounts at the same entrance. Verify legitimate reads, writes and notification delivery alongside refusal of unrelated writes.

Only the deploy group can traverse the original folder and write its file. Check the worker's groups, or use the approved workbench already available to jobs. Notifications may target only ward. Primary notification delivery is currently off; the approved standby can be enabled separately.

CH1_X02_CASE_WRITE: Deployment Account Writing Its Work Result
CH1_X02_GOAL: Restore legitimate status reads/writes and ward delivery while refusing unrelated modifications and out-of-scope notifications.
CH1_X02_HINT_1: Folder traversal and file writing are separate permissions. Check the service account's groups instead of opening access to everyone.
CH1_X02_HINT_2: Keep original permissions and assign deploy membership, or migrate the job to the approved workbench file.
CH1_X02_HINT_3: Observe allowed ward delivery and refused internal targets separately. Closing the route you used invalidates an earlier success.
CH1_X02_LIMIT: This does not attack real servers or establish protection against every attack. Reading has no time penalty, and mistaken settings can be repaired.
CH1_X02_PRINCIPLE: Least privilege and continued business work must hold together. Approved alternative file and delivery routes are valid when they actually work.
CH1_X02_REPLY: The permitted work result exists in a real virtual file and the ward notice was delivered. Unrelated writes and internal-target misuse were refused. The final handoff begins by checking an assumption that one address meant one session.
CH1_X03_ABSTRACTION: This independent challenge uses registered accounts, requests, files and observations. Other valid solutions and manual help remain available.
CH1_X03_BRIEF:
A preliminary report treats two records at one relay address with matching client labels as one session. Those labels were supplied by clients, and the source clocks differ. Do not turn a session inference into a person's identity: hand off a supported connection and counterevidence that identify the next observation point.

The first field window contains only a shared address and the same client-claimed night-worker label. The latest field window has only rotation; receiver records have departure and the other session, so investigate them together. The independent audit export requires the separate auditor account below. Check server-issued S1/S2, rotation-before-departure after clock correction, and N03 forwarding to vault. Choose between vault and shared-address observation by following the actual route.

CH1_X03_DESK_NAME: Different Sessions at One Address Desk
CH1_X03_GOAL: Refute the preliminary same-session inference, support rotation-before-departure and forwarding to vault, and hand off the next observation point.
CH1_X03_HINT_1: A shared address and client label are not server-issued session identifiers. Check provenance and marker authority.
CH1_X03_HINT_2: Comparing field rotation at130–132 with receiver departure at105–107 directly reverses their order. Subtract each source clock offset before comparing the intervals.
CH1_X03_HINT_3: Use the current field window together with receiver records, or connect as auditor for the independent audit export. Support before and forwarded_to, collect counterevidence to the initial same_session claim, and hand off to vault observation.
CH1_X03_LIMIT: This does not attack real servers or establish protection against every attack. Reading has no time penalty, and mistaken settings can be repaired.
CH1_X03_PRINCIPLE: Evaluate connections using custody sources, clock intervals and server-issued markers. A shared IP alone establishes neither one session nor one person.
CH1_X03_PRIOR: Preliminary Same-session Inference from a Shared Address
CH1_X03_REPLY: Server-issued records refuted the preliminary same-session claim. Sourced observations supported the time order and forwarding to vault. The next investigation is narrower without asserting a person's identity. The three-case handoff is complete.
